author: Bobby Grayson
description: FILE: Leanactors/Examples/TtlLive.lean (imports Fair, TtlProof, SupervisorLive; wired into Leanactors.lean after TtlProof). Theorems: gen_advances_or_clears (WeakFair (.timer 0), WeakFair (.run 0), Good start: a cache holding some v at gen g eventually takes a run 0 step that leaves gen g: .cache none (g+1) [after body], .cache (some x) (g+1) [message processed], or dead [put 0]); gen_changes_or_clears (requested shape: gen != g, or .cache none _, or dead); gen_advances; gen_advances_or_clears_timers (under forall i, WeakFair (.timer i), one instantiation); gen_advances_or_clears_env (from SysReachEnv init); value_eventually_expires (if no message is processed at gen g and the cache does not die, it reaches .cache none (g+1)). HONESTY: the literal corollary 'if the generation never changes after t then the value clears' is NOT stated because its premise is unsatisfiable along any fair run: the after body itself moves to g+1 (the receive is re-entered), so 'generation never changes' can only mean idling forever, which fairness forbids; the honest premise is 'no message is processed at generation g and the cache does not die' (value_eventually_expires), whose witness is wit_quiet. Non-vacuity: Good needs none of Inv (the environment may deliver anything); s0_reachable/premise_reachable (.cache (some 5) 1 via env put 5, run 0, timer 0 (stale gen-0 fires), run 0); wit = explicit fair run alternating timer 0 / run 0 that expires the value at time 2 (fair_run_exists, wit_expires, wit_clears). FAIRNESS FORM: WeakFair (.timer 0) means 'the oldest pending timer eventually fires'; it is implied by forall i WeakFair (.timer i) (the watchdog piece's premise for TimerFair) and the rank argument on the timer's position does the index shifting. The watchdog's SysRun.TimerFair 0 (after_run g) would also do; not used here. README Status paragraph: change 'The supervisor and the lock also have a liveness property proved along fair runs' to 'The supervisor, the lock and the ttl cache also have a liveness property proved along fair runs'. README table row Ttl: append '; liveness: a held value is cleared by its after-timer unless a message is processed first (or put 0 kills the cache)'. README Layout row to add after TtlProof: | Leanactors/Examples/TtlLive.lean | Liveness: under weak fairness of the oldest pending timer and of run 0, a held value does not stay at its generation (gen_advances_or_clears: the after body clears it, a message re-arms at g+1, or put 0 kills the cache); two rank_leads_to_of_step stages on the timer's position in timers and on after_run g's position in the cache's mailbox; Good = links/signals empty, pid 0 a cache, the current generation's timer in flight (Armed), kept by every step and every delivery; explicit fair witness run wit |. NOTES round-5 bullet: 'Ttl liveness (TtlLive.lean, ~1060 lines): the safety file said the cache never holds 0; the liveness file says a held value does not stay: the timer of the current generation is always in flight (Armed, half of Good; the safety invariant Inv is not needed at all), it fires under fairness of the oldest timer (rank = its position in timers, which only grows by appends and shrinks by firings), then run 0 pops it (rank = its position in the mailbox, stale timers ahead of it are consumed with the state unchanged). Lean lessons: an exported constructor alias (Msg.after_run through export Gen.Ttl (Msg)) does not resolve, write Gen.Ttl.Msg.after_run; nomatch h, x, y parses x y as discriminants; inside theorem Good.init the bare name init is Good.init.' Counts: +~1060 hand-written lines, +~55 theorems (remeasure with find/grep as before).
